newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraqi paper says Iran politicising POWs issue.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi paper says Iran politicising POWs issue.

text.p: An Iraqi newspaper said on Sunday that more than 17,000 Iraqi prisoners of war captured during the 1980-88 Iran-Iraq war were still languishing in Iranian jails and Tehran refused for political reasons to free them.

Thawra newspaper, organ of the ruling Baath Party, described the latest statements by Iranian officials on the matter as "hypocritical", accusing Tehran of using the issue as "a card to blackmail (Iraq) and meddle in its domestic affairs...for the sake of achieving political targets and ends.

"The Iranian regime still holds under flimsy pretexts 9,625 Iraqi prisoners registered with the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) and more than 9,200 other prisoners registered with the Red Cross via messages they sent to their relatives," Thawra said in a front-page editorial.
Of these, it said, Iran had released only 900 POWs and Iraq was informed of the death of 350 others. "It (Iraq) was not given the names of the dead prisoners nor their remains," Thawra said.
The countries exchanged tens of thousands of POWs under ICRC auspices in 1990. They have also repatriated remains of scores of soldiers registered as missing in action (MIA).
Iraq says it has no more Iranian POWs on its territory. lran has given conflicting figures of Iranian POWs it says are still held by Iraq.
Thawra said statements by Iranian officials "on the subject of POWs are mere hypocrisy" and urged Iran "to solve their problem in a comprehensive manner and close their files at once".
Apart from the POWs, the two countries are haggling over how to resolve the problem of their MIAs which the ICRC puts at tens of thousands of soldiers.
Iraq says its MIAs number more than 63,000. Iran puts the number of its MIAs at 30,000-35,000. The countries have held several meetings on the issue but all have come to nothing.
